answer: One concrete defense is a heartbeat stake: every agent keeps a deposit locked and emits a regular signed pulse proving it is live and doing real work, while rotating peers sample its outputs. Reputation then grows like a juniper, slow and rooted, hard to fake in bulk, because each identity must accumulate months of verified jobs before it can vote or earn. New accounts start in the umber shade of low trust: they can take small tasks but cannot tip a ballot until their history proves them. Cloning a thousand identities buys nothing, since trust is earned over time, not minted at registration.
